project_scope.note: Current canonical website anchor is Ashe juniper; Taxodium remains family-context material until promoted.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with foliage plus cone type. Ashe juniper has tiny opposite scale leaves on angled branchlets and fleshy blue seed cones.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Cupressaceae foliage may be scale-, awl-, or needle-like depending on genus and life stage.
family_diagnostics.reproduction: No true flowers or fruits. Pollen cones and seed cones are gymnosperm strobili.
family_diagnostics.cones: Juniperus seed-cone scales become fleshy and coalesced; Taxodium has woody globose cones.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: A juniper 'berry' is a fleshy seed cone, not a fruit.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Ashe juniper teaches the biggest Cupressaceae mental-model shift: the blue 'berry' is actually a fleshy cone.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the adult foliage
steps.look_for: Tiny overlapping/opposite scale leaves on short angled branchlets.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the fastest local Juniperus foliage pattern.

steps.title: 2 · Call the blue structure a seed cone
steps.look_for: Blue-glaucous fleshy structures formed from coalesced cone scales.
steps.why_it_matters: Corrects the common 'juniper berry' misconception and reinforces gymnosperm reproduction.

steps.title: 3 · Read the whole architecture
steps.look_for: Evergreen woody architecture with fibrous/peeling bark and dense scale foliage.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the close-up cone/leaf characters back to the whole plant.

steps.title: 4 · Add the reproductive counterpart
steps.look_for: Small pollen cones are separate structures from the larger fleshy female seed cones.
steps.why_it_matters: Builds the male/female conifer-reproduction model needed for Cupressaceae.

comparisons.title: Cupressaceae vs Pinaceae
comparisons.rule: Local junipers lack pine-style needle fascicles and classic free-scaled pine cones; their seed cones may be fleshy.

comparisons.title: Cupressaceae vs Taxaceae
comparisons.rule: Taxaceae typically presents one seed associated with a fleshy aril; Cupressaceae retains a true multi-scale seed cone and lacks an aril.

visual_lesson.caveat: Taxodium is the crucial deciduous/linear-leaved family exception and should be added as soon as a canonical image package is promoted.
